nodes.name: Round randomness
nodes.statement: A round configuration is a function r colon V to V times V times V assigning to every agent v an ordered triple of samples, each drawn independently and uniformly from V, with replacement (an agent may sample itself, or the same agent twice --- harmless, since a majority of three Boolean values is always well defined). Let R_n = V^3V denote the (finite) set of round configurations, with the uniform probability measure.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:round}
  
  
  A \emph{round configuration} is a function $r \colon V \to V \times V
  \times V$ assigning to every agent $v$ an ordered triple of \emph{samples},
  each drawn independently and uniformly from $V$, \emph{with} replacement
  (an agent may sample itself, or the same agent twice --- harmless, since a
  majority of three Boolean values is always well defined). Let
  $R_n = V^{3V}$ denote the (finite) set of round configurations, with the
  uniform probability measure.
nodes.clean_text: A round configuration is a function r colon V to V times V times V assigning to every agent v an ordered triple of samples, each drawn independently and uniformly from V, with replacement (an agent may sample itself, or the same agent twice --- harmless, since a majority of three Boolean values is always well defined). Let R_n = V^3V denote the (finite) set of round configurations, with the uniform probability measure.
nodes.label: def:round

nodes.name: Majority step
nodes.statement: For an opinion-1 set I subseteq V and r in R_n, \[ step(I,r) \;=\; \\, v in V : at least two of r(v)'s three coordinates lie in I \,\. \] Each agent independently samples 3 agents and adopts the majority of their current opinions.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:step}
  
  
  
  For an opinion-$1$ set $I \subseteq V$ and $r \in R_n$,
  \[
    \mathrm{step}(I,r) \;=\; \{\, v \in V : \text{at least two of } r(v)\text{'s three
    coordinates lie in } I \,\}.
  \]
  Each agent independently samples $3$ agents and adopts the majority of
  their current opinions.

nodes.label: def:step

nodes.name: Process
nodes.statement: Fix a horizon T in N and an initial set I_0 subseteq V. The sample space is Omega = R_n^\,T with the uniform (i.i.d.) measure. For r = (r_0,dots,r_T-1) in Omega define I_t+1 = step(I_t, r_t). We write X_t = |I_t| and U_t = n - X_t. In the formalization, a trajectory is a List of round configurations and run\ I\ l folds step over the list l.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:process}
  
  
  
  Fix a horizon $T \in \N$ and an initial set $I_0 \subseteq V$. The sample
  space is $\Omega = R_n^{\,T}$ with the uniform (i.i.d.) measure. For
  $r = (r_0,\dots,r_{T-1}) \in \Omega$ define $I_{t+1} =
  \mathrm{step}(I_t, r_t)$. We write $X_t = |I_t|$ and $U_t = n - X_t$. In
  the formalization, a trajectory is a \texttt{List} of round configurations
  and $\mathrm{run}\ I\ l$ folds \texttt{step} over the list $l$.

In the formalization, a trajectory is a List of round configurations and run\ I\ l folds step over the list l.
nodes.label: def:process

nodes.name: Monotone coupling
nodes.statement: For a fixed round r, the map I mapsto step(I,r) is monotone: I subseteq I' implies step(I,r) subseteq step(I',r); iterating over a trajectory, run is monotone in the same sense. This is purely combinatorial (no probability involved).
conclusions: For a fixed round r, the map I mapsto step(I,r) is monotone: I subseteq I' implies step(I,r) subseteq step(I',r); iterating over a trajectory, run is monotone in the same sense.
This is purely combinatorial (no probability involved).
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:mono}
  
  
  
  For a \emph{fixed} round $r$, the map $I \mapsto \mathrm{step}(I,r)$ is
  monotone: $I \subseteq I'$ implies $\mathrm{step}(I,r) \subseteq
  \mathrm{step}(I',r)$; iterating over a trajectory, $\mathrm{run}$ is
  monotone in the same sense. This is purely combinatorial (no probability
  involved).

nodes.label: lem:mono

nodes.statement: Unlike the push protocol, where the analogous monotonicity (Lemma~ there) is load-bearing throughout, here the per-round probabilistic estimates below (Lemmas~, , etc.) are instead stated and proved directly for any set I satisfying a hypothesis on |I|, using monotonicity of the real polynomial p of Section~ on [0,1] rather than a reference-embedding argument via Lemma~. Lemma~ is recorded because it is the exact analogue of the push protocol's structural fact, but it is not otherwise used by the chain of lemmas leading to the main theorem.

nodes.name: 3-majority reaches consensus in $O(\log n)$ rounds w.h.p.
nodes.statement: Let n be such that log n ge 30 (in particular n ge 2), let I_0 subseteq V with |I_0| ge tfrac35 n, and set \[ T \;=\; 10 + (T_2a(n) + 2), T_2a(n) = ceil6log n. \] Then Pr[\, I_T = V \,] \;ge\; 1 - dfrac500n.
assumptions: Let n be such that log n ge 30 (in particular n ge 2), let I_0 subseteq V with |I_0| ge tfrac35 n, and set \[ T \;=\; 10 + (T_2a(n) + 2), T_2a(n) = ceil6log n.
\] Then Pr[\, I_T = V \,] \;ge\; 1 - dfrac500n.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{thm:main}
  
  
  
  Let $n$ be such that $\log n \ge 30$ (in particular $n \ge 2$), let
  $I_0 \subseteq V$ with $|I_0| \ge \tfrac35 n$, and set
  \[
    T \;=\; 10 + (T_{2a}(n) + 2), \qquad T_{2a}(n) = \ceil{6\log n}.
  \]
  Then $\Pr[\, I_T = V \,] \;\ge\; 1 - \dfrac{500}{n}$.

nodes.label: thm:main

nodes.statement: As in the push protocol's write-up, the threshold log n ge 30 and the constant 500 are deliberately crude: the proof is organized to keep every inequality an easy direct computation, not to be sharp. Reaching this modest, two-digit threshold on log n (rather than an astronomically large one) relies on two ingredients in Section~: a degree-11 instance of the generic exponential-vs-power bound (Lemma~), and a log-log bound tangent at a reference point near the threshold itself rather than at the fixed point e (Lemma~). It is known (Doerr--Goldberg--Minder--Sauerwald--Scheideler 2011; Becchetti--Clementi--Natale--Pasquale--Silvestri, SODA 2015) that an initial imbalance of only Theta(sqrtnlog n) already suffices for O(log n)-round consensus w.h.p.; reaching that sharp threshold requires tracking the process on the scale of its own standard deviation throughout, a substantially more delicate multi-scale argument. Here a constant-fraction initial imbalance keeps every step to a single, reusable Chernoff bound (Section~) applied at a handful of explicit parameters.

  the constant $500$ are deliberately crude: the proof is organized to keep
  every inequality an easy direct computation, not to be sharp. Reaching
  this modest, two-digit threshold on $\log n$ (rather than an
  astronomically large one) relies on two ingredients in
  Section~\ref{sec:ineq}: a degree-$11$ instance of the generic
  exponential-vs-power bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:exppow}), and a log-log bound
  tangent at a reference point near the threshold itself rather than at the
  fixed point $e$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:loglog}). It is known
  (Doerr--Goldberg--Minder--Sauerwald--Scheideler 2011;
  Becchetti--Clementi--Natale--Pasquale--Silvestri, SODA 2015) that an
  initial imbalance of only $\Theta(\sqrt{n\log n})$ already suffices for
  $O(\log n)$-round consensus w.h.p.; reaching that sharp threshold
  requires tracking the process on the scale of its own standard deviation
  throughout, a substantially more delicate multi-scale argument. Here a
  constant-fraction initial imbalance keeps every step to a single,
  reusable Chernoff bound (Section~\ref{sec:chernoff}) applied at a handful
  of explicit parameters.

nodes.name: Average
nodes.statement: For a finite type alpha and f colon alpha to R, avg(f) := bigl(sum_a f(a)bigr)/|alpha| is the expectation of f under the uniform distribution on alpha.

\label{def:avg}
  
  
  For a finite type $\alpha$ and $f \colon \alpha \to \R$,
  $\mathrm{avg}(f) := \bigl(\sum_a f(a)\bigr)/|\alpha|$ is the expectation of
  $f$ under the uniform distribution on $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Trajectory expectation
nodes.statement: Exactly as in the push protocol: expList\ alpha\ T\ F is the expectation of a functional F of a trajectory of T i.i.d.\ uniform draws from alpha, defined by recursion on T (the head draw is averaged out first), so conditioning on the first round is a definitional unfolding.

\label{def:expList}
  
  
  
  Exactly as in the push protocol: $\mathrm{expList}\ \alpha\ T\ F$ is the
  expectation of a functional $F$ of a trajectory of $T$ i.i.d.\ uniform
  draws from $\alpha$, defined by recursion on $T$ (the head draw is
  averaged out first), so conditioning on the first round is a definitional
  unfolding.

nodes.name: Independence over a product space
nodes.statement: New relative to the push protocol, since that development only ever averaged over a single uniform draw at a time. For finite types beta,delta and g colon betatoR, hcolondeltatoR: avg(p mapsto g(p_1)h(p_2)) = avg(g)\,avg(h) over the product betatimesdelta (avg\_mul\_prod), with marginal consequences avg\_fst\_mul/avg\_snd\_mul. Iterating over a Fin\ n-indexed product (avg\_prod\_pi): for f colon Fin\ n to gamma to R, \[ avgBigl(x mapsto textstyleprod_i f_i(x_i)Bigr) \;=\; prod_i avg(f_i) \] over x colon Fin\ n to gamma --- the discrete, measure-theory-free form of ``coordinate projections on a product space are independent,'' with a one-coordinate marginal corollary (avg\_eval). This is exactly the independence fact that lets the n agents' per-round updates be combined into a single concentration bound (Section~).
conclusions: New relative to the push protocol, since that development only ever averaged over a single uniform draw at a time.

For finite types beta,delta and g colon betatoR, hcolondeltatoR: avg(p mapsto g(p_1)h(p_2)) = avg(g)\,avg(h) over the product betatimesdelta (avg\_mul\_prod), with marginal consequences avg\_fst\_mul/avg\_snd\_mul.

Iterating over a Fin\ n-indexed product (avg\_prod\_pi): for f colon Fin\ n to gamma to R, \[ avgBigl(x mapsto textstyleprod_i f_i(x_i)Bigr) \;=\; prod_i avg(f_i) \] over x colon Fin\ n to gamma --- the discrete, measure-theory-free form of ``coordinate projections on a product space are independent,'' with a one-coordinate marginal corollary (avg\_eval).
This is exactly the independence fact that lets the n agents' per-round updates be combined into a single concentration bound (Section~).
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:indep}
  
  
  
  \textbf{New relative to the push protocol}, since that development only
  ever averaged over a single uniform draw at a time. For finite types
  $\beta,\delta$ and $g \colon \beta\to\R$, $h\colon\delta\to\R$:
  $\mathrm{avg}(p \mapsto g(p_1)h(p_2)) = \mathrm{avg}(g)\,\mathrm{avg}(h)$
  over the product $\beta\times\delta$ (\texttt{avg\_mul\_prod}), with
  marginal consequences \texttt{avg\_fst\_mul}/\texttt{avg\_snd\_mul}.
  Iterating over a $\mathrm{Fin}\ n$-indexed product
  (\texttt{avg\_prod\_pi}): for $f \colon \mathrm{Fin}\ n \to \gamma \to \R$,
  \[
    \mathrm{avg}\Bigl(x \mapsto \textstyle\prod_i f_i(x_i)\Bigr)
      \;=\; \prod_i \mathrm{avg}(f_i)
  \]
  over $x \colon \mathrm{Fin}\ n \to \gamma$ --- the discrete,
  measure-theory-free form of ``coordinate projections on a product space
  are independent,'' with a one-coordinate marginal corollary
  (\texttt{avg\_eval}). This is exactly the independence fact that lets the
  $n$ agents' per-round updates be combined into a single concentration
  bound (Section~\ref{sec:chernoff}).

Iterating over a Fin\ n-indexed product (avg\_prod\_pi): for f colon Fin\ n to gamma to R, \[ avgBigl(x mapsto textstyleprod_i f_i(x_i)Bigr) \;=\; prod_i avg(f_i) \] over x colon Fin\ n to gamma --- the discrete, measure-theory-free form of ``coordinate projections on a product space are independent,'' with a one-coordinate marginal corollary (avg\_eval). This is exactly the independence fact that lets the n agents' per-round updates be combined into a single concentration bound (Section~).

conclusions: For a,b,c in \0,1\: mathbf 1[a+b+cge2] = ab+bc+ac-2abc.
Applied pointwise to the three samples of a fixed agent, this expresses the majority indicator as a polynomial in the three membership indicators.

\label{lem:majpoly}

nodes.name: Per-agent contribution
nodes.statement: Y_maj(I,v,s) in \0,1\ is 1 iff a majority of the sample triple s lies in I (independent of v, kept as a function of v to match the shape the Chernoff bound of Section~ expects). Then |step(I,r)| = sum_v Y_maj(I,v,r(v)) (card\_step\_eq\_sum): the per-agent, \0,1\-valued decomposition that Section~'s tail bounds need.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:Ymaj}
  
  
  
  $Y_{\mathrm{maj}}(I,v,s) \in \{0,1\}$ is $1$ iff a majority of the sample
  triple $s$ lies in $I$ (independent of $v$, kept as a function of $v$ to
  match the shape the Chernoff bound of Section~\ref{sec:chernoff} expects).
  Then $|\mathrm{step}(I,r)| = \sum_v Y_{\mathrm{maj}}(I,v,r(v))$
  (\texttt{card\_step\_eq\_sum}): the per-agent, $\{0,1\}$-valued
  decomposition that Section~\ref{sec:chernoff}'s tail bounds need.
nodes.clean_text: Y_maj(I,v,s) in \0,1\ is 1 iff a majority of the sample triple s lies in I (independent of v, kept as a function of v to match the shape the Chernoff bound of Section~ expects). Then |step(I,r)| = sum_v Y_maj(I,v,r(v)) (card\_step\_eq\_sum): the per-agent, \0,1\-valued decomposition that Section~'s tail bounds need.
nodes.label: def:Ymaj

nodes.name: Exact one-round drift
nodes.statement: Conditionally on a fixed I with |I|=m, the next count X_t+1 = |step(I,r)| satisfies \[ E_r[X_t+1] \;=\; n\,p(x), p(x) := 3x^2-2x^3, x = m/n, \] proved exactly (no approximation) via Lemma~, Definition~ and the independence toolkit of Lemma~ (each pairwise/triple product of membership indicators over distinct coordinates of the product space Tgt3\ n factors by avg\_mul\_prod).
conclusions: Conditionally on a fixed I with |I|=m, the next count X_t+1 = |step(I,r)| satisfies \[ E_r[X_t+1] \;=\; n\,p(x), p(x) := 3x^2-2x^3, x = m/n, \] proved exactly (no approximation) via Lemma~, Definition~ and the independence toolkit of Lemma~ (each pairwise/triple product of membership indicators over distinct coordinates of the product space Tgt3\ n factors by avg\_mul\_prod).
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:drift}
  
  
  
  Conditionally on a fixed $I$ with $|I|=m$, the next count
  $X_{t+1} = |\mathrm{step}(I,r)|$ satisfies
  \[
    \E_r[X_{t+1}] \;=\; n\,p(x), \qquad p(x) := 3x^2-2x^3, \qquad x = m/n,
  \]
  proved exactly (no approximation) via Lemma~\ref{lem:majpoly},
  Definition~\ref{def:Ymaj} and the independence toolkit of
  Lemma~\ref{lem:indep} (each pairwise/triple product of membership
  indicators over distinct coordinates of the product space
  $\mathrm{Tgt3}\ n$ factors by \texttt{avg\_mul\_prod}).
nodes.clean_text: Conditionally on a fixed I with |I|=m, the next count X_t+1 = |step(I,r)| satisfies \[ E_r[X_t+1] \;=\; n\,p(x), p(x) := 3x^2-2x^3, x = m/n, \] proved exactly (no approximation) via Lemma~, Definition~ and the independence toolkit of Lemma~ (each pairwise/triple product of membership indicators over distinct coordinates of the product space Tgt3\ n factors by avg\_mul\_prod).
nodes.label: lem:drift

For one Robin Hood transfer between colours a and b, the expectation, as a function of the mass theta of a (with a and b sharing a fixed total s), is nondecreasing on [s/2,s]: its derivative is a sum over agents, and swapping a and b for all agents and then for one agent pairs its terms into products of two factors with the same sign. A chain of transfers (the Hardy--Littlewood--P\'olya construction) leads from p to q when q is sorted and the partial sums of p dominate those of q; sorting and relabelling the colours, under which Schur-convex observables are invariant, reduce the general case to this one.

For $\varepsilon>0$, $\mathrm{Phase2}(\varepsilon)$ is the proposition (Theorem~3.1 of
\cite{BCNPT16}, Theorem~8 of \cite{BCEKMN17}): there are $C,N$ such that for $n\ge N$, from any
configuration with colours in $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ and $k\le n^{1/3-\varepsilon}$ colours,

$T\ge C(k^2\sqrt{\log n}+k\log n)(k+\log n)$ rounds with probability at most $1/n$.

``w.h.p.''\ is $1-O(n^{-\lambda})$ for some $\lambda>0$, which gives the form $1/n$ by repeating
the phase a constant number of times; the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:mo-phase2} gives the form
$1/n$ directly.

nodes.name: Population protocols with input and output
nodes.statement: A population protocol has an input function I : X to Q, an output function O : Q to \0, 1\ and a transition function delta : Q times Q to Q times Q. An encounter of an ordered pair (u, v) of distinct agents replaces their states p, q by delta(p, q); reachability is the reflexive-transitive closure of encounters. A configuration is output-stable with output b if in every configuration reachable from it every agent outputs b.

A configuration is output-stable with output b if in every configuration reachable from it every agent outputs b.

nodes.name: Stable computation
nodes.statement: A protocol stably computes a predicate varphi on input count vectors if, for every nonempty population and every input assignment iota, every configuration reachable from I circ iota can reach an output-stable configuration with output varphi of the input counts. A predicate is stably computable if a protocol with finitely many states stably computes it.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:stable}

A protocol stably computes a predicate $\varphi$ on input count vectors if, for every nonempty
population and every input assignment $\iota$, every configuration reachable from $I \circ \iota$
can reach an output-stable configuration with output $\varphi$ of the input counts. A predicate is
stably computable if a protocol with finitely many states stably computes it.
nodes.clean_text: A protocol stably computes a predicate varphi on input count vectors if, for every nonempty population and every input assignment iota, every configuration reachable from I circ iota can reach an output-stable configuration with output varphi of the input counts. A predicate is stably computable if a protocol with finitely many states stably computes it.
nodes.label: def:stable

nodes.name: Protocols are networks
nodes.statement: The transitions p + q to delta_1(p, q) + delta_2(p, q) that change \p, q\ form a count-conserving bimolecular network whose reachable count vectors are the counts of the configurations reachable in the protocol. Hence every stably computable predicate, and in particular every Boolean combination of threshold and remainder predicates, is stably decided by such a network.
conclusions: The transitions p + q to delta_1(p, q) + delta_2(p, q) that change \p, q\ form a count-conserving bimolecular network whose reachable count vectors are the counts of the configurations reachable in the protocol.
Hence every stably computable predicate, and in particular every Boolean combination of threshold and remainder predicates, is stably decided by such a network.

\label{thm:transfer}

The transitions $p + q \to \delta_1(p, q) + \delta_2(p, q)$ that change $\{p, q\}$ form a
count-conserving bimolecular network whose reachable count vectors are the counts of the
configurations reachable in the protocol. Hence every stably computable predicate, and in
particular every Boolean combination of threshold and remainder predicates, is stably decided by
such a network.

convergence probabilities.

\label{lem:tail}

Probability is monotone in the event. An observable $f\le1$ with $f(b)<1$ at a
point of positive weight has expectation $<1$. Markov's inequality
$\Pr(X\ge c)\le\E X/c$ for $X\ge0$, $c>0$; in particular
$\Pr(\sum_iY_i(\omega_i)\ge1)\le\sum_i\E Y_i$ for nonnegative coordinates. One

$1-\E[\mathrm{bad}]$ when $\mathrm{bad}\ge0$ is at least $1$ on every miss. If
$f\le Kf$, then $n\mapsto K^nf(a)$ is nondecreasing; in particular the occupation
probability of an absorbing event is nondecreasing in time. Finally
$e^{-2\log n}=1/n^2$ for $n\ge1$, and $\log n>0$ forces $n\ge1$.

nodes.name: The uniformized SIR chain
nodes.statement: Let beta,gammainmathbb N. A configuration assigns to each of N agents a compartment S, I or R; X=(S,I,R)/N are the scaled counts. One step draws (u,v) uniformly in [N]^2 and one of beta+gamma equally likely clocks: on one of the beta infection clocks an infected u infects a susceptible v, on one of the gamma recovery clocks an infected u recovers. This is the continuous-time chain (S+Ito2I at rate beta SI/N, Ito R at rate gamma I) uniformized at rate (beta+gamma)N. The deviation probability is the probability that \|X_k-x(k/((beta+gamma)N))\|_infty>theta for some kle n.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:kurtz}

Let $\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb N$. A configuration assigns to each of $N$ agents a compartment
$S$, $I$ or $R$; $X=(S,I,R)/N$ are the scaled counts. One step draws $(u,v)$ uniformly in
$[N]^2$ and one of $\beta+\gamma$ equally likely clocks: on one of the $\beta$ infection clocks an
infected $u$ infects a susceptible $v$, on one of the $\gamma$ recovery clocks an infected $u$
recovers. This is the continuous-time chain ($S+I\to2I$ at rate $\beta SI/N$, $I\to R$ at rate
$\gamma I$) uniformized at rate $(\beta+\gamma)N$. The deviation probability is the probability
that $\|X_k-x(k/((\beta+\gamma)N))\|_\infty>\theta$ for some $k\le n$.

This is the continuous-time chain (S+Ito2I at rate beta SI/N, Ito R at rate gamma I) uniformized at rate (beta+gamma)N. nodes.name: Rumor-spreading processes
nodes.statement: A rumor-spreading process on n nodes is a Markov kernel on the set S of informed nodes under which informed nodes stay informed. For a round started from S, informProb(S,x) is the probability that x is informed after the round and cov(S,x,y) the covariance of the events that x and y are. The tail of the spreading time is notYet(m,t,S)=Pr[fewer than m nodes informed after t rounds from S]=Pr[T(|S|,m)>t]; expected times are bounded through all partial sums of sum_tPr[T>t]. Homogeneity (Definition~6) is defined but not assumed.

which informed nodes stay informed. For a round started from $S$, $\mathrm{informProb}(S,x)$ is

the events that $x$ and $y$ are. The tail of the spreading time is

}S]=\Pr[T(|S|,m)>t]$; expected times are bounded through all partial sums of

Hence push satisfies the upper growth conditions with gamma=1, a=frac12 and the upper shrinking conditions with rho=1, a=frac2e, g=frac12; pull and push--pull satisfy the growth conditions with gamma=1, a=0 and gamma=2, a=frac34, and the double exponential shrinking conditions with ell=2, a=1, g=alpha=frac12 and fast finishing with tau=frac12 (all with b=c=0, f=frac12).

Hence push satisfies the upper growth conditions with gamma=1, a=frac12 and the upper shrinking conditions with rho=1, a=frac2e, g=frac12; pull and push--pull satisfy the growth conditions with gamma=1, a=0 and gamma=2, a=frac34, and the double exponential shrinking conditions with ell=2, a=1, g=alpha=frac12 and fast finishing with tau=frac12 (all with b=c=0, f=frac12).

\label{lem:rumor-protocol-conditions}

$1-(1-\frac1n)^k$ (push), $\frac kn$ (pull), $1-(1-\frac1n)^k(1-\frac kn)$ (push--pull);
distinct uninformed nodes are nonpositively correlated (independent for pull). Hence push
satisfies the upper growth conditions with $\gamma=1$, $a=\frac12$ and the upper shrinking
conditions with $\rho=1$, $a=\frac2e$, $g=\frac12$; pull and push--pull satisfy the growth
conditions with $\gamma=1$, $a=0$ and $\gamma=2$, $a=\frac34$, and the double exponential

Let $V$ be an observable of a Markov kernel and $(g_i)$, $(\delta_i)$ sequences with
$\delta_i\ge0$. If from every state with $V\ge g_i$ the observable falls below $g_{i+1}$ in one
round with probability at most $\delta_i$, then from a state with $V\ge g_0$ it is below $g_t$
after $t$ rounds with probability at most $\sum_{i<t}\delta_i$ (the round-by-round form of
Lemmas~42 and~50). For a rumor-spreading process: if one round multiplies the expected number of
informed nodes by at most $\mu$, then $\Pr[T(|S|,m)\le t]\le\mu^t|S|/m$; and if every state with
fewer than $m'$ informed nodes reaches $m$ within $t$ rounds with probability at most $B$, then
$\Pr[T(|S|,m)\le s+t]\le\Pr[T(|S|,m')\le s]+B$.

With two values this is 2-Choices: a node keeps its value unless both samples hold the other one.

nodes.statement: Take C=128 and chain one-round moves, each failing with probability at most n^-2, through four segments: the gap grows by a factor 5/4 per round until the minority is below n/4 (O(log(n/Delta)) rounds); six rounds bring the minority below n/8; it then shrinks quadratically, mmapstoapprox 3m^2/n (Bernstein), down to 512log n (O(loglog n) rounds); eight more rounds give consensus. nodes.name: Two-sample voting on a graph
nodes.statement: On a simple graph G, in a round every vertex samples two neighbours independently and uniformly at random (with replacement) and adopts the median of its own opinion and the two sampled ones; with two opinions it adopts the sampled opinion when the two samples agree. For a majority opinion a, the minority B is the set of vertices holding another opinion. E(S,T) is the number of ordered pairs (u,v)in Stimes T of adjacent vertices, so E(S,S)=2|E(S)|.

nodes.name: Adaptive adversary
nodes.statement: An adversary maps the list of rounds played so far (the current one last) and the output of the median rule in the current round to a new configuration; it is F-bounded if it recolours at most F nodes, and it uses values of S if every value it writes lies in S. The run against the adversary applies, in every round, the median rule and then the adversary. More generally, a perturbed run is any function of the rounds played so far that starts at x and, after every round, differs from the output of the median rule in at most F nodes. A configuration is in almost consensus on b with K exceptions if at most K nodes hold a value other than b; almost stable consensus during the times T_0,dots,T_0+H means almost consensus on the same value b at all these times.

nodes.name: Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary
nodes.statement: There is a constant C>0 such that, whenever log nge C and CFlesqrt n: let S be a set of m legal values containing the values of a configuration x. Against every F-bounded adversary that only writes values of S, and for every Hge0, almost stable consensus with C(F+log n) exceptions holds during the times lceil Clog nrceil,dots,lceil Clog nrceil+H, except with probability at most (m-1)(Clog n+H)/n^2.
conclusions: There is a constant C>0 such that, whenever log nge C and CFlesqrt n: let S be a set of m legal values containing the values of a configuration x.

Against every F-bounded adversary that only writes values of S, and for every Hge0, almost stable consensus with C(F+log n) exceptions holds during the times lceil Clog nrceil,dots,lceil Clog nrceil+H, except with probability at most (m-1)(Clog n+H)/n^2.

\label{thm:median-adv}

There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$ and $CF\le\sqrt n$: let $S$ be a set
of $m$ legal values containing the values of a configuration $x$. Against every $F$-bounded

$C(F+\log n)$ exceptions holds during the times $\lceil C\log n\rceil,\dots,\lceil C\log n\rceil+H$,
except with probability at most $(m-1)(C\log n+H)/n^2$.

nodes.statement: Take C=2^20. All values of the run lie in S. For every legal value b, the threshold umapsto[ble x_u] of the run is a perturbed run of 2-Choices with the same budget, because the median commutes with monotone maps and thresholding does not increase the Hamming distance. If, for every legal b above the minimum m_0, the threshold run stays in almost consensus on some c_b with K exceptions, let w be the largest legal value with w=m_0 or c_w=true: the nodes below w are exceptions of the threshold at w, and the nodes above w are exceptions of the threshold at the next legal value, so the run is in almost consensus on w with 2K exceptions. Conclude with the internal bound of Theorem~ and a union bound over the m-1 thresholds.

nodes.name: $k$-party 2-Choices
nodes.statement: Colours lie in any type with decidable equality. In a round every node samples two nodes uniformly at random (independently, with replacement) and adopts their colour if the two samples hold the same colour; otherwise it keeps its own. c_i is the number of nodes of colour i, and the number of nodes whose two samples both hold i is denoted twice_i.

nodes.statement: Consensus configurations are fixed; c_i'le c_i+twice_i, so an extinct colour stays extinct. On two colours the rule is the median of the own colour and the two samples. For the same rounds, every node that holds true in the binary median process started from the indicator of colour i holds colour i.
conclusions: Consensus configurations are fixed; c_i'le c_i+twice_i, so an extinct colour stays extinct.

nodes.statement: Choose a permutation tau of the nodes sending every node of colour c to a node of colour b. For every node v, the sample pairs that make v end in colour c are at most as many as those that make tau(v) end in colour b: a node of another colour adopts a colour of size m on the m^2 pairs with both samples on it, a node of that colour keeps it on the n^2-S+m^2 pairs that do not agree on another colour, and both counts increase with m. Choose a permutation of the sample pairs embedding the first set into the second. The induced bijection of rounds preserves the uniform distribution and maps the rounds with c_c'ge t into the rounds with c_b'ge t. nodes.name: The phases
nodes.statement: Fix m, lambda, Lambda and let q = 1 + 1/(6lambda), B = n^1/4log n. Growth phase i: c_m > frac23 n, or M(c) = \m\, c_m ge n/lambda and s(c) ge Lambda q^i. Saturation phase j: n - c_m < max\frac n3 (frac1718)^j,\ B\. Consensus: c_m = n.

\label{def:phases}
  
  
  
  Fix $m$, $\lambda$, $\Lambda$ and let $q = 1 + 1/(6\lambda)$,
  $B = n^{1/4}\log n$.
  \emph{Growth phase $i$}: $c_m > \frac23 n$, or $M(c) = \{m\}$,
  $c_m \ge n/\lambda$ and $s(c) \ge \Lambda q^i$.
  \emph{Saturation phase $j$}:
  $n - c_m < \max\{\frac n3 (\frac{17}{18})^j,\ B\}$.
  \emph{Consensus}: $c_m = n$.

\label{lem:hit_absorb}
  
  
  Let $P$ be an absorbing event of a finite Markov chain. If from every state of $B$ the chain is
  in $P$ after $T$ steps with probability at least $1 - \varepsilon$, then from any state it is in
  $P$ at time $t + T$ with probability at least $\Pr(T_B \le t) - \varepsilon$. If moreover from
  every state the chain is in $P$ after $T_1$ steps with probability at least $1 - \varepsilon$,
  and from $a$ after $T_0$ steps with probability at least $1 - \delta$, then from $a$ it is in
  $P$ after $T_0 + T_1$ steps with probability at least $1 - \delta\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Rules, $\Delta$, $\delta$ and solvers
nodes.statement: A rule is conservative if it returns one of its inputs. It has the clear-majority property if it returns the majority color whenever two inputs agree. For colors r ne b, Delta_r counts the orderings of (r,r,b) on which the rule returns r. For distinct r,g,b, delta_c counts the orderings of (r,g,b) on which it returns c; the rule is uniform if delta_r = 2 for all distinct triples. It is an (s,varepsilon)-solver if from every coloring whose unique plurality color m has bias at least s, consensus on m is eventually reached with probability at least 1-varepsilon.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:good_rules}
  
  
  
  A rule is \emph{conservative} if it returns one of its inputs. It has the
  \emph{clear-majority} property if it returns the majority color whenever two
  inputs agree. For colors $r \ne b$, $\Delta_r$ counts the orderings of
  $(r,r,b)$ on which the rule returns $r$. For distinct $r,g,b$, $\delta_c$
  counts the orderings of $(r,g,b)$ on which it returns $c$; the rule is
  \emph{uniform} if $\delta_r = 2$ for all distinct triples. It is an
  \emph{$(s,\varepsilon)$-solver} if from every coloring whose unique plurality
  color $m$ has bias at least $s$, consensus on $m$ is eventually reached with
  probability at least $1-\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.8(a), clear majority
nodes.statement: Let 8 mid n. With only colors r, b present and x the fraction of r, a node adopts r with probability p(x), where p(x) - x = x(1-x)bigl(x(Delta_r - 2) + (1-x)(2 - Delta_b)bigr). If Delta_r le 2 le Delta_b, the number of r nodes is a supermartingale, so from 5n/8 nodes of r (bias n/4) consensus on r has probability at most 5/8 at every time: the rule is not an (n/4, 1/4)-solver. Consequently, for an (n/4, 1/4)-solver and every pair r ne b, either Delta_r = Delta_b = 3 or Delta_r, Delta_b le 1.

\label{thm:4_8_a}
  
  
  
  Let $8 \mid n$. With only colors $r, b$ present and $x$ the fraction of $r$,
  a node adopts $r$ with probability $p(x)$, where
  $p(x) - x = x(1-x)\bigl(x(\Delta_r - 2) + (1-x)(2 - \Delta_b)\bigr)$. If
  $\Delta_r \le 2 \le \Delta_b$, the number of $r$ nodes is a supermartingale,
  so from $5n/8$ nodes of $r$ (bias $n/4$) consensus on $r$ has probability at
  most $5/8$ at every time: the rule is not an $(n/4, 1/4)$-solver.
  Consequently, for an $(n/4, 1/4)$-solver and every pair $r \ne b$, either
  $\Delta_r = \Delta_b = 3$ or $\Delta_r, \Delta_b \le 1$.

  appear equally often, so each is chosen with the same probability.

nodes.name: Push step
nodes.statement: For an informed set I subseteq V and a round configuration omega in R_n, the next informed set is \[ step(I,omega) \;=\; I \,cup\, omega(I) \;=\; I cup \omega(v) : v in I\. \] (Only informed nodes actually transmit; letting all nodes draw a target and ignoring the choices of uninformed nodes is an equivalent and formalization-friendlier convention.)
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:step}
  
  
  
  For an \emph{informed set} $I \subseteq V$ and a round configuration
  $\omega \in R_n$, the next informed set is
  \[
    \mathrm{step}(I,\omega) \;=\; I \,\cup\, \omega(I)
    \;=\; I \cup \{\omega(v) : v \in I\}.
  \]
  (Only informed nodes actually transmit; letting \emph{all} nodes draw a
  target and ignoring the choices of uninformed nodes is an equivalent and
  formalization-friendlier convention.)

nodes.name: Process
nodes.statement: Fix a horizon T in N and a start vertex v_0 in V. The sample space is Omega = R_n^\,T (uniform measure, i.e.\ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds). For omega = (omega_0,dots,omega_T-1) in Omega define I_0(omega) = \v_0\ and I_t+1(omega) = step(I_t(omega), omega_t) for 0 le t < T. We write m_t = |I_t| and U_t = n - m_t for the numbers of informed and uninformed nodes. Since Omega is finite, all probabilities are finite ratios and all expectations are finite sums; ``conditioning on I_t'' means partitioning Omega according to the first t coordinates. In the formalization, a trajectory is simply a List of round configurations and run\ I\ l folds step over the list l.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:process}
  
  
  
  Fix a horizon $T \in \N$ and a start vertex $v_0 \in V$. The sample space
  is $\Omega = R_n^{\,T}$ (uniform measure, i.e.\ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds).
  For $\omega = (\omega_0,\dots,\omega_{T-1}) \in \Omega$ define
  $I_0(\omega) = \{v_0\}$ and
  $I_{t+1}(\omega) = \mathrm{step}(I_t(\omega), \omega_t)$ for $0 \le t < T$.
  We write $m_t = |I_t|$ and $U_t = n - m_t$ for the numbers of informed and
  uninformed nodes. Since $\Omega$ is finite, all probabilities are finite
  ratios and all expectations are finite sums; ``conditioning on $I_t$''
  means partitioning $\Omega$ according to the first $t$ coordinates. In the
  formalization, a trajectory is simply a \texttt{List} of round
  configurations and $\mathrm{run}\ I\ l$ folds \texttt{step} over the list
  $l$.

We write m_t = |I_t| and U_t = n - m_t for the numbers of informed and uninformed nodes. Since Omega is finite, all probabilities are finite ratios and all expectations are finite sums; ``conditioning on I_t'' means partitioning Omega according to the first t coordinates. In the formalization, a trajectory is simply a List of round configurations and run\ I\ l folds step over the list l.

nodes.name: Push protocol informs $K_n$ in $O(\log n)$ rounds w.h.p.
nodes.statement: Let n ge 2, let v_0 in V, and set \[ T_1 \;=\; ceil117 log n + 23, T_2 \;=\; ceil6 log n, T \;=\; T_1 + T_2 . \] Then Prbigl[\, I_T = V \,bigr] \;ge\; 1 - frac2n. In particular all nodes are informed after O(log n) rounds with high probability.
assumptions: Let n ge 2, let v_0 in V, and set \[ T_1 \;=\; ceil117 log n + 23, T_2 \;=\; ceil6 log n, T \;=\; T_1 + T_2 .
\] Then Prbigl[\, I_T = V \,bigr] \;ge\; 1 - frac2n.
conclusions: In particular all nodes are informed after O(log n) rounds with high probability.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{thm:main}
  
  
  
  Let $n \ge 2$, let $v_0 \in V$, and set
  \[
    T_1 \;=\; \ceil{117 \log n} + 23, \qquad
    T_2 \;=\; \ceil{6 \log n}, \qquad
    T \;=\; T_1 + T_2 .
  \]
  Then $\Pr\bigl[\, I_T = V \,\bigr] \;\ge\; 1 - \frac{2}{n}$.
  In particular all nodes are informed after $O(\log n)$ rounds with high
  probability.

nodes.label: thm:main

nodes.name: Trajectory expectation
nodes.statement: For a finite type alpha, expList\ alpha\ T\ F is the expectation of a functional F of a trajectory of T i.i.d.\ uniform draws from alpha, defined by recursion on T: the head draw is averaged out first, i.e.\ expList\ alpha\ 0\ F = F(\,[]\,) and expList\ alpha\ (T+1)\ F = avgbigl(a mapsto expList\ alpha\ T\ (l mapsto F(a :: l))bigr). This makes ``conditioning on the first round'' a definitional unfolding rather than a measure-theoretic construction.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:expList}
  
  
  
  For a finite type $\alpha$, $\mathrm{expList}\ \alpha\ T\ F$ is the
  expectation of a functional $F$ of a trajectory of $T$ i.i.d.\ uniform
  draws from $\alpha$, defined \emph{by recursion on $T$}: the head draw is
  averaged out first, i.e.\ $\mathrm{expList}\ \alpha\ 0\ F = F(\,[]\,)$ and
  $\mathrm{expList}\ \alpha\ (T{+}1)\ F
    = \mathrm{avg}\bigl(a \mapsto \mathrm{expList}\ \alpha\ T\ (l \mapsto
    F(a :: l))\bigr)$.
  This makes ``conditioning on the first round'' a definitional unfolding
  rather than a measure-theoretic construction.
nodes.clean_text: For a finite type alpha, expList\ alpha\ T\ F is the expectation of a functional F of a trajectory of T i.i.d.\ uniform draws from alpha, defined by recursion on T: the head draw is averaged out first, i.e.\ expList\ alpha\ 0\ F = F(\,[]\,) and expList\ alpha\ (T+1)\ F = avgbigl(a mapsto expList\ alpha\ T\ (l mapsto F(a :: l))bigr). This makes ``conditioning on the first round'' a definitional unfolding rather than a measure-theoretic construction.
nodes.label: def:expList

nodes.name: Second-order lower bound, ``Bonferroni''
nodes.statement: For 0 le x le 1 and m in N: \[ 1-(1-x)^m \;ge\; mx - binomm2x^2 \;ge\; mxBigl(1-fracmx2Bigr), \] and consequently mx/2 le 1-(1-x)^m whenever mx le 1.
conclusions: For 0 le x le 1 and m in N: \[ 1-(1-x)^m \;ge\; mx - binomm2x^2 \;ge\; mxBigl(1-fracmx2Bigr), \] and consequently mx/2 le 1-(1-x)^m whenever mx le 1.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:bonferroni}
  
  
  
  For $0 \le x \le 1$ and $m \in \N$:
  \[
    1-(1-x)^m \;\ge\; mx - \binom{m}{2}x^2 \;\ge\; mx\Bigl(1-\frac{mx}{2}\Bigr),
  \]
  and consequently $mx/2 \le 1-(1-x)^m$ whenever $mx \le 1$.

nodes.name: Markov's inequality, finite uniform version
nodes.statement: Let Omega be a finite nonempty set with the uniform measure, f colon Omega to R with f ge 0, and a > 0. Then Pr[f ge a] le E[f]/a. In particular, if f takes values in N, then Pr[f ne 0] le E[f].

conclusions: Then Pr[f ge a] le E[f]/a.
In particular, if f takes values in N, then Pr[f ne 0] le E[f].
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:markov}
  
  
  
  Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with the uniform measure,
  $f \colon \Omega \to \R$ with $f \ge 0$, and $a > 0$. Then
  $\Pr[f \ge a] \le \E[f]/a$. In particular, if $f$ takes values in $\N$,
  then $\Pr[f \ne 0] \le \E[f]$.

nodes.label: lem:markov

nodes.name: Enough good rounds force half-saturation
nodes.statement: Let L in N satisfy (9/8)^L > n/2. If the informed set never exceeds n/2 up to time T_1, then along that trajectory m_T_1 ge (9/8)^goodCount cdot m_0: every good round multiplies m_t by ge 9/8 and every round is non-decreasing (Lemma~), so goodCount ge L would force m_T_1 > n/2, a contradiction — hence goodCount < L Rightarrow m_T_1 le n/2 is impossible to rule out only via the deterministic growth bound stated here.

\label{lem:force}
  
  
  
  Let $L \in \N$ satisfy $(9/8)^L > n/2$. If the informed set never exceeds
  $n/2$ up to time $T_1$, then along that trajectory
  $m_{T_1} \ge (9/8)^{\mathrm{goodCount}} \cdot m_0$: every good round
  multiplies $m_t$ by $\ge 9/8$ and every round is non-decreasing
  (Lemma~\ref{lem:mono}), so $\mathrm{goodCount} \ge L$ would force
  $m_{T_1} > n/2$, a contradiction — hence
  $\mathrm{goodCount} < L \Rightarrow m_{T_1} \le n/2$ is impossible to rule
  out only via the deterministic growth bound stated here.

nodes.name: Lower bound; Theorem~8
nodes.statement: There is C>0 such that, for every n with log nge C, every k with Ckle(n/log n)^1/6 and every configuration x without undecided nodes: for every T with CTlemd(x), after T rounds every colour has at most Cn/md(x) nodes with probability at least 1-C/n; and for every T with C(T+1)lemd(x), all nodes hold the same colour after T rounds with probability at most C/n. nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:double-cover}

The graph $\tilde G=G\times K_2$ has vertices $(a,i)$, $a\in V$, $i\in\{0,1\}$, and
$(a,i)\sim(b,j)$ iff $a\sim b$ in $G$ and $i\neq j$. Swapping the layers is an automorphism,
degrees are those of $G$, and $\mathrm{vol}\,\tilde G=2\,\mathrm{vol}\,G$.

nodes.statement: On the two-vertex graph, every vertex must copy the other vertex. The alternating coloring flips each round and returns after two rounds; neither coloring is constant. Thus connectedness alone is insufficient.
